sentences.text:
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner as well as the learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
Perused the CRLMC application as well as the prayer made therein.

3. By filing the present CRLMC application under section 482 Cr.P.C. which corresponds to Section 528 of BNSS, 2023, the Petitioner has sought for a direction to the learned trial court to conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner at the outset contended that initially Banki P.S.Case No.214 of 2020 was registered for commission of offence under section 363/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

After conclusion of the investigation, Charge Sheet has been filed under sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n), 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code read with Sections 6 & 17 of Complainant/Informant vs ) State Of Odisha on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2083672/
1 POCSO Act.

He further contended that although timeline has been stipulated in the POCSO Act,
trial is continuing since last several years.
On such ground, learned counsel for the Petitioner contended that the trial court be directed to conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible.
4. Learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State on the other hand contended that the learned trial court is taking all possible steps to conclude the trial at the earliest.
He further contended that although timeline has been stipulated in the POCSO Act, however due to non- attendance of witnesses, the trial could not be concluded.
On such ground learned Additional Standing Counsel contended that no further direction is necessary to conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible.

5. Having heard learned counsels for the respective parties and after careful examination of the background facts of the present case and further keeping in view the fact that in the POCSO Act there exists a time limit, this Court disposes of the present application with an observation that the trial court shall make every endeavour to conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of six months from the date of communication of certified copy of this order.
6.
With the aforesaid observation the CRLMC is disposed of.

( A.K. Mohapatra) Judge RKS Designation: AR-CUM-Senior Secretary Complainant/Informant vs ) State Of Odisha on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2083672/
